content_voiceover: This is the same ICC hierarchy, now annotated with the key differences from the WHO classification, a favorite source of trick questions. First, WHO eliminated the blast cutoff entirely for AML with defining genetic alterations, meaning even blasts below 10% can qualify, whereas ICC still requires at least 10% blasts for that category. Second, WHO does not use TP53 mutation as its own hierarchical branch point the way ICC does. Third, WHO's myelodysplasia-related gene mutation list does not include RUNX1, so that gene is ICC-specific for this category. Fourth, for myelodysplasia-related cytogenetic abnormalities, WHO does not list trisomy 8 or del 20q, while ICC does not include del 11q, monosomy 13, or del 13q, so the two systems' cytogenetic lists are not interchangeable. Finally, WHO frames its terminal category around AML defined by differentiation rather than ICC's not-otherwise-specified label. On boards, expect questions that hinge on exactly these discrepancies, so know which classification system the question is asking about before you answer.
keypoints: WHO: no blast cutoff for genetically-defined AML
WHO doesn't branch on TP53; ICC does
RUNX1 in ICC's MDS-gene list, not WHO's
Cytogenetics differ: WHO omits +8/del(20q); ICC omits del(11q)/-13/del(13q)
keypoint_voiceover: The exam trap is mixing up WHO and ICC criteria. WHO drops the blast cutoff for genetic AML and doesn't use TP53 as a branch point; ICC does both, and their myelodysplasia-related gene and cytogenetic lists differ slightly too.
